Situation1: There is a scheduled family gathering on the calendar.
Expectation2: Be friendly and polite in daily interactions
Situation2: A brief encounter in the corridor leads to a simple hello and smile.
Story:
I was bustling around the kitchen, preparing snacks for the family gathering that had been on the calendar for weeks. My daughter had reminded me how much the grandkids were looking forward to our time together, and I wanted everything to be perfect. Just as I was about to set the table, I realized I’d forgotten to pick up the special juice my grandson loves. I hurried out, hoping to make it back before everyone arrived. 

As I stepped into the corridor, I nearly bumped into Mrs. Lee, my neighbor. She smiled and greeted me warmly, as she always did. I knew she liked to chat for a few minutes whenever we met, and I didn’t want to seem rude or unfriendly. But I could feel the minutes ticking away, the pressure mounting to get back before my family arrived. I stood there, torn between the expectation to be a warm, attentive grandparent and the desire to be a considerate, friendly neighbor. My heart raced as I tried to decide what to do next.
